comparisons.peer_topic: Use and Definition of Managed Basis Non-GAAP Measures
comparisons.peer_summary: JPMorgan uses 'managed basis' non-GAAP financial measures for management review, which start with reported U.S. GAAP results and include reclassifications to present total net revenue on an FTE basis, making tax-exempt sources comparable to taxable ones for year-to-year comparability.
comparisons.comparison: Citi and JPMorgan both utilize a 'managed basis' framework to present financial results for segments and the firm overall, adjusting reported GAAP results to exclude certain items for management review. Citi specifically reports its 'All Other' revenues on a managed basis, stating these revenues decreased 20%. JPMorgan defines 'managed basis' as starting with reported U.S. GAAP results and including reclassifications, such as presenting revenue on a full-time equivalent (FTE) basis to make tax-exempt sources comparable to taxable ones. Both disclosures confirm the use of this non-GAAP adjusted measure for segment and corporate reporting, though JPM's disclosure is definitional whereas Citi's is a specific performance result.
